issues.t: Camshaft position sensor can melt and start a fire (recall)
issues.sym: A burning plastic smell or smoke from the engine bay, sometimes with a check engine light, stalling or a no-start.
issues.why: The camshaft position sensor, which tells the engine computer where the camshaft is, can overheat and melt. The heat can spread to the cam cover and the sensor wiring and could start a fire. Recall 04V-357 replaces the sensor and adds a fuse. It is by far the most-reported Lanos problem.
issues.next: If you smell burning or see smoke, pull over, turn the engine off and get away from the car. Daewoo's US dealer network closed, and many owners could not get the recall done, so call NHTSA's recall line with your VIN and ask a shop to check the sensor and wiring.

issues.t: Timing belt or tensioner fails and bends valves
issues.sym: The engine suddenly dies while driving and cranks but won't start, sometimes after a slapping or rattling noise from the belt area.
issues.why: The 1.6L engine is driven by a rubber timing belt. If the belt or its tensioner pulley fails, the valves hit the pistons and bend. Owners report failures around 70,000 to 77,000 miles, and some blame a defective tensioner arm.
issues.next: If you don't have proof it was done, replace the timing belt, tensioner and idler pulleys now. Owners suggest doing it about every 50,000 miles and changing the water pump at the same time. If the belt has already snapped, don't keep cranking. Have it towed and ask for a compression test.

issues.sym: Coolant puddles, a sweet smell, steam from under the hood, or the temperature gauge climbing. One owner's gauge gave no warning until the thermostat housing cracked.
issues.why: Owners report a cracked plastic thermostat housing, a snapped coolant hose, a leaking water pump or heater hose, and intake manifold gasket leaks. Overheating can blow the head gasket and ruin the engine.
issues.next: Check the coolant level when the engine is cold. If the gauge climbs or you see steam, pull over and turn the engine off right away. Driving even a short distance while overheating can destroy the engine.

issues.t: Engine stalls or shuts off without warning
issues.sym: The engine cuts out while driving, braking or parking, or won't start at all. The check engine light may be on.
issues.why: Owners trace it to the camshaft or crankshaft position sensors, a throttle body fault, damaged wiring, or water getting into and ruining the engine computer.
issues.next: If it stalls, steer to safety. Steering and brakes get heavy with the engine off. Have the codes read and the sensor wiring checked. Also make sure the cam sensor recall was done.

issues.t: Rough idle or stalling when cold
issues.sym: The engine idles roughly, surges or stalls until it warms up, and may be hard to start cold.
issues.why: Owners trace it to a sticking EGR valve, a dirty throttle body or fuel injectors, a clogged fuel filter, or a faulty idle control motor.
issues.next: Have the codes read. Cleaning the EGR valve and throttle body and replacing the fuel filter are cheap first steps that often help.

issues.t: Brakes wear quickly, grind or calipers stick
issues.sym: Grinding from the front brakes, pads and rotors wearing out every few thousand miles, a burning smell, or the car pulling when braking.
issues.why: Owners report fast pad and rotor wear, warped front rotors and seized calipers. A sticking caliper keeps a pad dragging, which wears it out and overheats the brake.
issues.next: Have the brakes inspected, including caliper slide pins and pistons. If you smell burning or the car pulls hard when braking, get it checked before driving far.

issues.t: Headlights cut out from melted connectors
issues.sym: One or both headlights go out while driving, flicker, or stop working. The plug behind the bulb may look browned or melted.
issues.why: Heat from the bulb breaks down the headlight connector until it loses contact. Owners mention a service bulletin that changed the bulb type to reduce this.
issues.next: Don't drive at night with a headlight out. Have the connector and wiring replaced, not just the bulb, and use the bulb type the shop recommends.

issues.sym: The automatic downshifts suddenly at highway speed, bangs into gear, slips into neutral on hills, or leaks fluid. Some manual cars grind in third gear.
issues.why: Owners report internal wear and fluid leaks. Some needed a replacement transmission.
issues.next: Check the transmission fluid level and look for leaks. If it slips or drops gears, drive gently and have it diagnosed before it leaves you stranded.

issues.sym: A roaring or humming that gets louder with speed, coming from the rear. Some owners also notice looseness at a wheel.
issues.why: The rear wheel bearings wear out. Owners report both failing, and failures returning after earlier repairs.
issues.next: Have the bearings checked soon. A badly worn bearing can overheat and, in extreme cases, let the wheel wobble.

issues.t: Brake lights stop working from a failed switch
issues.sym: The brake lights don't come on, or come on only sometimes. A failing switch can also make the shifter stick in Park.
issues.why: The brake light switch under the pedal wears out or sticks. One owner was rear-ended because the brake lights did not work.
issues.next: Have someone watch the brake lights while you press the pedal. The switch is a cheap part, so replace it right away.

issues.sym: Clunking when shifting or accelerating, heavy vibration, or the engine moving around. In one case the engine came loose and the car stalled.
issues.why: An engine mount bracket can crack and break off, letting the engine shift in its compartment.
issues.next: Have the mounts inspected if you hear clunks on takeoff. Don't keep driving if the engine is visibly loose.

issues.sym: The car drifts left or right on a straight road and needs constant steering correction.
issues.why: Owners report alignment problems and worn parts. Uneven tire pressure or a sticking brake can also cause it.
issues.next: Check tire pressures, then get an alignment and have the brakes and wheel bearings checked if it keeps pulling.

issues.t: Floor wiring harness can chafe and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine runs poorly or suddenly stalls, often without a clear pattern.
issues.why: A wiring harness under the front passenger carpet rubs against a seam in the floor and gets damaged by passengers' feet. Recall 01V-020 moves and secures the harness.
issues.next: Ask a shop to look under the passenger carpet for chafed wires, especially if the car stalls at random. Check the VIN for open recalls.

issues.sym: Clunking or a wobble from a wheel, especially after hard braking.
issues.why: Alloy wheels were made without steel inserts around the bolt holes, so the bolts can work loose. Recall 99V-336 re-torques the bolts to a new spec.
issues.next: If you hear clunking from a wheel, stop and check the wheel bolts. Have all bolts torqued to the correct spec.

issues.sym: Usually none, although some owners report the airbag light staying on.
issues.why: The car did not meet the federal standard for head protection from the passenger airbag cover. Recall 02V-131 installs energy-absorbing mounting brackets. Many owners could not get it done after dealers closed.
issues.next: Ask NHTSA or a shop to check your VIN for this recall. If the airbag light is on, have the system diagnosed.

issues.sym: Extra play or looseness in the steering wheel.
issues.why: The bushing that joins the steering wheel to the column can slip. Recall 98V-305 replaced the wheel with a revised one.
issues.next: If the steering wheel feels loose, have it inspected before driving more.

issues.t: Door side-impact pad in the wrong spot (recall)
issues.why: The side-impact pad inside the doors was placed toward the rear instead of the middle, which reduces hip protection in a side crash. Recall 99V-090 moves it.
issues.next: Ask for a VIN recall check. It is not urgent for daily driving, but it matters in a side crash.
